## Description

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind kep

#### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds KEP-1466, a design document for SLSA Build L1 provenance on Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.

Kueue releases currently lack any machine-verifiable provenance linking published images and Helm charts back to the source commit and build job. Issue kubernetes-sigs/kueue#1466 tracks this gap.

The KEP proposes attaching SLSA v1 provenance attestations to staging artifacts at build time, using Cloud Build as the build platform and Sigstore keyless signing (cosign + Fulcio + Rekor). The existing `kueue-sa` service account in the `k8s-staging-images` project is used as the build identity. kpromo already carries OCI referrers from staging to `registry.k8s.io` during promotion.

Artifacts covered: 5 container images (`kueue`, `kueueviz-backend`, `kueueviz-frontend`, `kueue-populator`, `kueue-priority-booster`) and 3 Helm charts.

Graduation: Alpha v0.21 → Beta v0.22 → Stable v0.23.

Related: kubernetes-sigs/kueue#1466
Related: kubernetes-sigs/kueue#17748

Note: prior related attempts — kubernetes-sigs/kueue#12287 (closed) and kubernetes-sigs/kueue#12313 (open). This KEP starts fresh, scoping to build-time staging provenance with Sigstore keyless signing.

cc @ctmphuongg (author of the prior attempt in kubernetes-sigs/kueue#12313)

#### Useful notes for your reviewer

This is a design-only PR (KEP + kep.yaml). No code changes.

`make verify` could not run locally — macOS requires `brew install gnu-sed` which is not installed. The change is documentation-only (KEP markdown files in `keps/`); no generated source files were modified.

+
+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+After each image and chart push, the staging build signs a SLSA v1 build provenance attestation as an OCI referrer.
+The signature uses the build's own workload identity.
+The image promoter verifies the attestation when present and carries it to the production registry, next to the promotion signature.
+Consumers verify the attestation against the build identity and the public Sigstore transparency log.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **SLSA** (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts): a framework that defines levels of build provenance assurance. This KEP targets SLSA Build L1, which requires a signed provenance statement from the build system.
+- **Sigstore**: an open-source project providing tools and infrastructure for signing and verifying software artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter.
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+- **OCI referrer**: an artifact attached to an existing image or chart via the OCI referrers API, allowing tools to discover signatures, attestations, and SBOMs associated with a digest without modifying the original artifact.
+- **cosign**: a Sigstore tool for signing and verifying container images and other OCI artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Fulcio / Rekor**: Sigstore components. Fulcio issues short-lived signing certificates tied to a workload identity (OIDC token). Rekor is the public transparency log where certificates and signatures are recorded and made auditable.
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue image they are running
+
+An admin wants to confirm that a running Kueue image was built from a known commit.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+They admit Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: slsaprovenance1
```

  <excerpt>citeturn0search2 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; Policy Controller v0.13.0 added support for the recently introduced Sigstore bundle format, which changes the way signatures and attestations are serialized and stored. ... If using Cosign to attest the image with `--new-bundle-format`, you’ll need to enable the bundle signature format in your `ClusterImagePolicy` using the `signatureFormat` field. ...         predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
  
  #### Sigstore bundle format #
  
  Policy Controller v0.13.0 added support for the recently introduced Sigstore bundle format, which changes the way signatures and attestations are serialized and stored. These changes were made starting in Cosign v2.4.0 to standardize the way Sigstore metadata is represented across multiple language clients and to align with the OCI 1.1 manifest referrers API.
  
  Currently only attestations, not plain signatures, are supported in the bundle format. If using Cosign to attest the image with `--new-bundle-format`, you’ll need to enable the bundle signature format in your `ClusterImagePolicy` using the `signatureFormat` field. For example:
      
      `apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
      kind: ClusterImagePolicy
      metadata:
        name: image-policy
      spec:
        images:
        - glob: &quot;**&quot;
        authorities:
        - keyless:
            url: https://fulcio.example.com
            identities:
              - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
                subject:
        signatureFormat: bundle
        attestations:
        - name: require-attestation
          predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
      `
  
  ### Configuring `static` authorities #
  
  Authorities can be `static` specifications. These are used for example when there are images that may not have any signatures or attestations (sidecar is one example of these). For these you can configure a `static` authority and you can define an action to take. Currently we support `pass` and `fail`, and when a `static` authority is evaluated, no signatures or attestations are checked, but instead the `action` specified defines whether the policy is validated or rejected.
  
  You can also use a generic catch-all CIP that matches all images. For example, if you want to allow all unsigned images through, but have certain images that must have signatures/attestations, you can then for those images create other CIP that is more restrictive, and since the CIP are all anded together they will then be required to meet all the CIP requirements.
  </excerpt>
  </source>

  <title>docs/content/en/policy-controller/overview.md at main · sigstore/docs · GitHub</title>
  <location>https://github.com/sigstore/docs/blob/main/content/en/policy-controller/overview.md</location>
  <excerpt>citeturn0search1 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 3 days ago; Policy Controller v0.13.0 added support for the recently introduced [Sigstore bundle format]({{&lt; relref &quot;about/bundle&quot; &gt;}}), which changes the way signatures and attestations are serialized and stored. ... If using Cosign to attest the image with `--new-bundle-format`, you&#39;ll need to enable the bundle signature format in your `ClusterImagePolicy` using the `signatureFormat` field. ...           predicateType: https://cosign.sigstore.dev/attestation/v1
  
  ## Configuring policy-controller `ClusterImagePolicy`
  
  `policy-controller` supports validation against multiple `ClusterImagePolicy` Kubernetes resources.
  
  A policy is enforced when an image pattern for the policy is matched against the image being deployed.
  
  Detailed field descriptions for the ClusterImagePolicy CRD.
  
  ### Configuring image patterns
  
  The `ClusterImagePolicy` specifies `spec.images` which specifies a list of `glob` matching patterns. These matching patterns will be matched against the image digest of PodSpec resources attempting to be deployed. Note that we use Duck typing here, so when we say PodSpec, we enforce these against higher level resources that result in pods, for example, Deployment, StatefulSet, etc. by default. You can configure these with `MatchResource` (see more below). Reason for this default is that if we only enforce at the Pod level, the user may be confused when their `Deployment` is accepted, yet later on the `Pod`s are unable to start due to policies blocking them.
      
  
  Each `keyless` authority can contain these properties:
  
    * `keyless.url`: specifies the Fulcio url
    * `keyless.ca-cert`: specifies `ca-cert` information for the `keyless` authority
      * `secretRef.name`: specifies the secret location name in the same namespace where `policy-controller` is installed.
  The first key value will be used in the secret for the `ca-cert`.
      * `data`: specifies the inline certificate data
    * `keyless.identities`: Identities must contain an array of `issuer` and the `subject` matching the certificate used to sign. There are variant fields `issuerRegExp` and `subjectRegExp` which support regular expressions.
      * `issuer`: specifies the issuer certificate was issued by. Regex patterns are supported through the `issuerRegExp` key.
      * `subject`: specifies the subject certificate was issued to. Regex patterns are supported through the `subjectRegExp` key.
  
  
  #### Sigstore bundle format
  
  Policy Controller v0.13.0 added support for the recently introduced [Sigstore bundle format]({{&lt; relref &quot;about/bundle&quot; &gt;}}), which changes the way signatures and attestations are serialized and stored. These changes were made [starting in Cosign v2.4.0]({{&lt; relref &quot;cosign/verifying/verify#new-bundle-format&quot; &gt;}}) to standardize the way Sigstore metadata is represented across multiple language clients and to align with the OCI 1.1 manifest referrers API.
  
  Currently only attestations, not plain signatures, are supported in the bundle format. If using Cosign to attest the image with `--new-bundle-format`, you&#39;ll need to enable the bundle signature format in your `ClusterImagePolicy` using the `signatureFormat` field. For example:
      
      apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
      kind: ClusterImagePolicy
      metadata:
        name: image-policy
      spec:
        images:
        - glob: &quot;**&quot;
        authorities:
        - keyless:
            url: https://fulcio.example.com
            identities:
              - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
                subject:
        signatureFormat: bundle
        attestations:
        - name: require-attestation
          predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
  
          ctlog:
            url: http://rekor.rekor-system.svc
          attestations:
          - name: custom-match-predicate
            predicateType: https://cosign.sigstore.dev/attestation/v1
            policy:
              type: rego
              data: |
                package sigstore
                default isCompliant = false
                isCompliant {
                  input.predicateType == &quot;https://cosign.sigstore.dev/attestation/v1&quot;
                  input.predicate == &quot;foobar e2e test&quot;
                }
  
  
  ### Configuring policy at the `ClusterImagePolicy` level.
  
  As discussed earlier, by specifying multiple `ClusterImagePolicy` creates an `AND` clause so that each `ClusterImagePolicy` must be satisfied for an admission, and having multiple `authorities` creates an `OR` clause so that any matching `authority` is considered a success, sometimes you may want more flexibility, for example, if you wanted to specify that at least 2 out of N signatures match, and for those you can create a single `ClusterImagePolicy` but craft a `policy` that then gets applied after a `ClusterImagePolicy` has been validated and at least one of the authorities matches.
      
      apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1alpha1
      kind: ClusterImagePolicy
      metadata:
        name: image-policy-objectmeta
      spec:
        images:
        - glob: &quot;ghcr.io/sigstore/timestamp-server**&quot;
        authorities:
        - static:
            action: pass
        policy:
          includeObjectMeta: true
          type: &quot;cue&quot;
          data: |
            metadata: &quot;labels&quot;: &quot;foo&quot;: &quot;bar&quot;
  
  ### Including TypeMeta for CIP level policies
  
  In order to include the TypeMeta, you have to explicitly configure the CIP.Spec.Policy to have `includeTypeMeta` set to `true`. For example, to configure a check that the resource is a Pod, you would configure your CIP like this:
      
      apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1alpha1
      kind: ClusterImagePolicy
      metadata:
        name: image-policy-typemeta
      spec:
        images:
        - glob: &quot;ghcr.io/sigstore/timestamp-server**&quot;
        authorities:
        - static:
            action: pass
        policy:
          includeTypeMeta: true
          type: &quot;cue&quot;
          data: |
            typemeta:
            sha256sum: 291534e501184200a3933969277403acf50582fbe73509571a5b73017e49a957
  
  NOTE: URLs are not automatically refreshed. They are fetched whenever a CIP changes (to simulate this you can update a label for example), or whatever the reconcile frequency is (by default 10 hours, but configurable).
  
  ### Controlling warn vs. enforce behaviour
  
  When creating a `ClusterImagePolicy` by default when a policy fails to meet the requirements, it will not be admitted. However, sometimes folks want to allow these through, but warn the user about the fact that this operation did not meet the criteria. For this you can use a `mode` configuration option for a specific policy. When set to `warn`, it will not block the admission, but instead will allow it through and emit a warning.
  
  For example:
      
      apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1alpha1
      kind: ClusterImagePolicy
      metadata:
        name: image-policy-keyless-warn
      spec:
        mode: warn
        images:
        - glob: registry.local:5000/policy-controller/demo*
        authorities:
        - keyless:
            url: http://fulcio.fulcio-system.svc
          ctlog:
            url: http://rekor.rekor-system.svc
  
  By specifying the `spec.mode` as `warn`, even if an image is found to be not compliant, it will be allowed through, but a warning is issued to the caller informing them that this is not a compliant image.
  
  ### Policies matching specific resource types and labels
  
  The `ClusterImagePolicy` supports a new field that defines which type of core resources a policy will enforce against the defined authorities for a given glob pattern.
  
  The following is an example of a `ClusterImagePolicy` that defines a list of resource types to enforce a policy for `pods` and `cronjobs`:
      
      apiVersion: cosigned.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
      kind: ClusterImagePolicy
      metadata:
        name: image-policy
      spec:
        match:
        - resource: jobs
          group: batch
          version: v1
        - resource: pods
          version: v1
        images:
        - glob: *
        authorities:
        - keyless:
            url: https://fulcio.mattmoor.dev/
            identities:
            - issuer: https://container.googleapis.com/v1/projects/myco-prod/locations/*/clusters/*
              subject: https://k8s.io/namespaces/*/serviceaccounts/*
      
          tlog:
            url: https://rekor.mattmoor.dev
  
  Besides the selection of specific types, the resources could also be selected using labels to filter them from other resources of the same type. </excerpt>
  </source>

  <title>Support arbitrary in-toto attestation predicate types in Sigstore Bundle verification · Issue #588 · sigstore/sigstore-rs · GitHub</title>
  <location>GitHub issue 588 in sigstore/sigstore-rs (link omitted to avoid creating a cross-reference)</location>
  <excerpt>citeturn0search3 [wordlim: 200] Published: 4 months ago; Crawled: 2 months ago; This image carries an SLSA provenance attestation (`https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`) as a Sigstore Bundle v0.3 OCI referrer. ...       --predicate-type &quot;https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1&quot; \
  
  # Support arbitrary in-toto attestation predicate types in Sigstore Bundle verification #588
  
  New issue
  
  Copy link
  
  New issue
  
  Copy link
  
  Open
  
  Open
  
  Support arbitrary in-toto attestation predicate types in Sigstore Bundle verification#588
  
  Copy link
  
  Labels
  
  enhancementNew feature or requestNew feature or request
  
  ## Description
  
  ryan-surname-p
  
  opened on Jun 22, 2026
  
  Issue body actions
  
  When verifying OCI images that carry Sigstore Bundle v0.3 referrers `sigstore-rs` hard-codes the accepted `predicateType` to `https://sigstore.dev/cosign/sign/v1`.
  
  This means that images with other valid attestation types — such as SLSA provenance (`https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`), SBOMs, or any other in-toto predicate — are rejected during `SignatureLayer` construction.
  
  This restriction should be removed so that any in-toto Statement v1 predicate type can be accepted.
  
  ## Motivation
  
  Some OCI artifacts are published with attestations that use predicate types other than `cosign/sign/v1`. </excerpt>
  </source>

  <title>GitHub - sigstore/policy-controller: Sigstore Policy Controller - an admission controller that can be used to enforce policy on a Kubernetes cluster based on verifiable supply-chain metadata from cosign · GitHub</title>
  <location>https://github.com/sigstore/policy-controller</location>
  <excerpt>citeturn0search4 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 3 weeks ago;             --image=ghcr.io/sigstore/cosign/cosign:v1.9.0 | jq) ... Sigstore Policy Controller - an admission controller that can be used to enforce policy on a Kubernetes cluster based on verifiable supply-chain metadata from cosign
  
  # Policy Controller
  
  The `policy-controller` admission controller can be used to enforce policy on a Kubernetes cluster based on verifiable supply-chain metadata from `cosign`.
  
  `policy-controller` also resolves the image tags to ensure the image being ran is not different from when it was admitted.
  
  See the installation instructions for more information.
  
  Today, `policy-controller` can automatically validate signatures and attestations on container images. Enforcement is configured on a per-namespace basis, and multiple keys are supported.
  
  We&#39;re actively working on more features here.
  
  For more information about the `policy-controller`, have a look at our documentation website here.
  
  ## Examples
  
  Please see the examples/ directory for example policies etc.
  
  ## Policy Testing
  
  This repo includes a `policy-tester` tool which enables checking a policy against various images.
  
  In the root of this repo, run the following to build:

+# KEP-1466: SLSA build provenance for Kueue release artifacts
+
+<!-- toc -->
+- [Summary](#summary)
+- [Motivation](#motivation)
+  - [Goals](#goals)
+  - [Non-Goals](#non-goals)
+- [Proposal](#proposal)
+  - [Terminology](#terminology)
+  - [User Stories](#user-stories)
+    - [Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue image they are running](#story-1-a-cluster-admin-cannot-tell-which-commit-built-the-kueue-image-they-are-running)
+    - [Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time](#story-2-a-platform-team-wants-to-reject-kueue-images-without-build-provenance-at-admission-time)
+  - [Notes/Constraints/Caveats](#notesconstraintscaveats)
+  - [Risks and Mitigations](#risks-and-mitigations)
+    - [A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases](#a-sigstore-outage-can-delay-staging-builds-and-releases)
+    - [Anyone who can act as the build identity can sign false provenance](#anyone-who-can-act-as-the-build-identity-can-sign-false-provenance)
+    - [An unattested artifact can be promoted during the transition period](#an-unattested-artifact-can-be-promoted-during-the-transition-period)
+    - [Consumers may assume L1 provenance gives stronger guarantees than it does](#consumers-may-assume-l1-provenance-gives-stronger-guarantees-than-it-does)
+- [Design Details](#design-details)
+  - [Attested artifacts](#attested-artifacts)
+  - [Build identity](#build-identity)
+  - [Attestation step](#attestation-step)
+  - [Provenance content](#provenance-content)
+  - [Failure handling](#failure-handling)
+  - [Promotion](#promotion)
+  - [Release candidates](#release-candidates)
+  - [Changes in other repositories](#changes-in-other-repositories)
+  - [Interactions](#interactions)
+  - [Test Plan](#test-plan)
+    - [Prerequisite testing updates](#prerequisite-testing-updates)
+    - [Unit tests](#unit-tests)
+    - [Integration tests](#integration-tests)
+    - [e2e tests](#e2e-tests)
+  - [Graduation Criteria](#graduation-criteria)
+    - [Alpha (v0.21)](#alpha-v021)
+    - [Beta (v0.22)](#beta-v022)
+    - [Stable (v0.23)](#stable-v023)
+- [Implementation History](#implementation-history)
+- [Drawbacks](#drawbacks)
+- [Alternatives](#alternatives)
+- [Future work ideas](#future-work-ideas)
+- [Appendix: SLSA, Sigstore, and the image promoter](#appendix-slsa-sigstore-and-the-image-promoter)
+<!-- /toc -->
+
+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+After each image and chart push, the staging build signs a SLSA v1 build provenance attestation as an OCI referrer.
+The signature uses the build's own workload identity.
+The image promoter verifies the attestation when present and carries it to the production registry, next to the promotion signature.
+Consumers verify the attestation against the build identity and the public Sigstore transparency log.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **SLSA** (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts): a framework that defines levels of build provenance assurance. This KEP targets SLSA Build L1, which requires a signed provenance statement from the build system.
+- **Sigstore**: an open-source project providing tools and infrastructure for signing and verifying software artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter.
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+- **OCI referrer**: an artifact attached to an existing image or chart via the OCI referrers API, allowing tools to discover signatures, attestations, and SBOMs associated with a digest without modifying the original artifact.
+- **cosign**: a Sigstore tool for signing and verifying container images and other OCI artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Fulcio / Rekor**: Sigstore components. Fulcio issues short-lived signing certificates tied to a workload identity (OIDC token). Rekor is the public transparency log where certificates and signatures are recorded and made auditable.
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue image they are running
+
+An admin wants to confirm that a running Kueue image was built from a known commit.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+They admit Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: slsaprovenance1
+```
+
+### Notes/Constraints/Caveats
+
+- The level achieved is SLSA Build L1.
+  The build writes its own provenance predicate, and build steps are not isolated from each other.
+- Attestations attach to the multi-arch index digest that the image promoter references.
+  Platform-specific manifests do not carry their own attestation.
+
+### Risks and Mitigations
+
+#### A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases
+
+A staging build cannot sign or verify while Sigstore is unavailable.
+Rerun the postsubmit after the outage.
+Until the promoter policy requires provenance, a missing attestation delays the attestation but does not block promotion.
+
+#### Anyone who can act as the build identity can sign false provenance
+
+Access to the service account is limited to staging project administrators and the Cloud Build pipeline.
+Consumers must pin both the signing identity and the issuer when they verify.
+Consumers must not treat L1 provenance as tamper-proof.
+
+#### An unattested artifact can be promoted during the transition period
+
+The promoter policy starts in warn mode, so an unattested artifact can still be promoted.
+Until the policy requires provenance, the in-build self-check is the enforcement point.
+
+#### Consumers may assume L1 provenance gives stronger guarantees than it does
+
+The consumer documentation, tracked separately, states the SLSA level and its limits.
+
+## Design Details
+
+This KEP changes no Kueue API, configuration, or controller behavior.
+
+### Attested artifacts
+
+| Artifact | Type | Phase |
+|---|---|---|
+| kueue | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-backend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-frontend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| Periodic build images (debug, importer, ray-mini) | Image | Not attested |
+| GitHub release assets | Binary and manifest | Future work |
+
+### Build identity
+
+The staging build runs as a dedicated service account, `kueue-sa`, in the staging project.
+The account already has Artifact Registry write access and OIDC token-creator permissions.
+The build obtains a Fulcio identity certificate from its ambient Google identity, so it needs no extra credentials.
+Consumers verify against the account's email address and the Google OIDC issuer.
+
+### Attestation step
+
+1. After the image and chart pushes complete, resolve each artifact's digest from its tag.
+2. Write a SLSA v1 predicate that records the source repository, git ref, git commit, builder identity, and build invocation ID.
+3. Sign the predicate as a Sigstore bundle OCI referrer, using the build's ambient workload identity.
+4. Verify the attestation against the same digest and identity as an in-build self-check.
+   Fail the build if verification fails.
+
+A local dry-run mode writes the predicate without signing.
+
+### Provenance content
+
+The predicate has this shape. Values in angle brackets vary per build:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "buildType": "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/RELEASE.md#staging-image-provenance-v1",
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    },
+    "resolvedDependencies": [
+      { "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue", "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" } }
+    ]
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" },
+    "metadata": { "invocationId": "https://console.cloud.google.com/cloud-build/builds/<build-id>?project=<project-number>" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+### Failure handling
+
+A failed attestation or self-check step fails the build with a non-zero exit code.
+The artifact stays in the staging registry without an attestation.
+Rerunning the postsubmit signs the artifact again.
+The earlier push stays in the registry, but the promoter does not promote it, because promotion acts only on digests that the current run references.
```

  **Correct the failure-handling claim about promotion selection.**
  
  The promotion flow selects a staging digest by tag, not by the current run. `promote_pull.sh` resolves `${STAGING_IMAGE_REGISTRY}/${image_name}:${version}` with `gcloud container images describe` and inserts the returned digest into `images.yaml`. +- **Fulcio / Rekor**: Sigstore components. Fulcio issues short-lived signing certificates tied to a workload identity (OIDC token). Rekor is the public transparency log where certificates and signatures are recorded and made auditable.
+

+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue image they are running
+

+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \

+

+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+

+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com

+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: slsaprovenance1
```

+- [Implementation History](#implementation-history)
+- [Drawbacks](#drawbacks)

+- [Appendix: SLSA, Sigstore, and the image promoter](#appendix-slsa-sigstore-and-the-image-promoter)

+
+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+After each image and chart push, the staging build signs a SLSA v1 build provenance attestation as an OCI referrer.
+The signature uses the build's own workload identity.
+The image promoter verifies the attestation when present and carries it to the production registry, next to the promotion signature.
+Consumers verify the attestation against the build identity and the public Sigstore transparency log.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **SLSA** (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts): a framework that defines levels of build provenance assurance. This KEP targets SLSA Build L1, which requires a signed provenance statement from the build system.
+- **Sigstore**: an open-source project providing tools and infrastructure for signing and verifying software artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter.
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+- **OCI referrer**: an artifact attached to an existing image or chart via the OCI referrers API, allowing tools to discover signatures, attestations, and SBOMs associated with a digest without modifying the original artifact.
+- **cosign**: a Sigstore tool for signing and verifying container images and other OCI artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Fulcio / Rekor**: Sigstore components. Fulcio issues short-lived signing certificates tied to a workload identity (OIDC token). Rekor is the public transparency log where certificates and signatures are recorded and made auditable.
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue image they are running
+
+An admin wants to confirm that a running Kueue image was built from a known commit.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+They admit Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: slsaprovenance1
+```
+
+### Notes/Constraints/Caveats
+
+- The level achieved is SLSA Build L1.
+  The build writes its own provenance predicate, and build steps are not isolated from each other.
+- Attestations attach to the multi-arch index digest that the image promoter references.
+  Platform-specific manifests do not carry their own attestation.
+
+### Risks and Mitigations
+
+#### A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases
+
+A staging build cannot sign or verify while Sigstore is unavailable.
+Rerun the postsubmit after the outage.
+Until the promoter policy requires provenance, a missing attestation delays the attestation but does not block promotion.
+
+#### Anyone who can act as the build identity can sign false provenance
+
+Access to the service account is limited to staging project administrators and the Cloud Build pipeline.
+Consumers must pin both the signing identity and the issuer when they verify.
+Consumers must not treat L1 provenance as tamper-proof.
+
+#### An unattested artifact can be promoted during the transition period
+
+The promoter policy starts in warn mode, so an unattested artifact can still be promoted.
+Until the policy requires provenance, the in-build self-check is the enforcement point.
+
+#### Consumers may assume L1 provenance gives stronger guarantees than it does
+
+The consumer documentation, tracked separately, states the SLSA level and its limits.
+
+## Design Details
+
+This KEP changes no Kueue API, configuration, or controller behavior.
+
+### Attested artifacts
+
+| Artifact | Type | Phase |
+|---|---|---|
+| kueue | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-backend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-frontend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| Periodic build images (debug, importer, ray-mini) | Image | Not attested |
+| GitHub release assets | Binary and manifest | Future work |
+
+### Build identity
+
+The staging build runs as a dedicated service account, `kueue-sa`, in the staging project.
+The account already has Artifact Registry write access and OIDC token-creator permissions.
+The build obtains a Fulcio identity certificate from its ambient Google identity, so it needs no extra credentials.
+Consumers verify against the account's email address and the Google OIDC issuer.
+
+### Attestation step
+
+1. After the image and chart pushes complete, resolve each artifact's digest from its tag.
+2. Write a SLSA v1 predicate that records the source repository, git ref, git commit, builder identity, and build invocation ID.
+3. Sign the predicate as a Sigstore bundle OCI referrer, using the build's ambient workload identity.
+4. Verify the attestation against the same digest and identity as an in-build self-check.
+   Fail the build if verification fails.
+
+A local dry-run mode writes the predicate without signing.
+
+### Provenance content
+
+The predicate has this shape. Values in angle brackets vary per build:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "buildType": "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/RELEASE.md#staging-image-provenance-v1",
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    },
+    "resolvedDependencies": [
+      { "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue", "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" } }
+    ]
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" },
+    "metadata": { "invocationId": "https://console.cloud.google.com/cloud-build/builds/<build-id>?project=<project-number>" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+### Failure handling
+
+A failed attestation or self-check step fails the build with a non-zero exit code.
+The artifact stays in the staging registry without an attestation.
+Rerunning the postsubmit signs the artifact again.
+The earlier push stays in the registry, but the promoter does not promote it, because promotion acts only on digests that the current run references.
```

  Corrected the failure-handling description. The previous claim ('promotion acts only on digests the current run references') was incorrect — promotion resolves the release tag to a digest, so it can select an unattested digest if the tag still points to the failed run's image. Updated text explains the warn-mode risk and that require mode prevents it.

+### Attestation step
+
+1. After the image and chart pushes complete, resolve each artifact's digest from its tag.
+2. Write a SLSA v1 predicate that records the source repository, git ref, git commit, builder identity, and build invocation ID.
+3. Sign the predicate as a Sigstore bundle OCI referrer, using the build's ambient workload identity.
+4. Verify the attestation against the same digest and identity as an in-build self-check.
+   Fail the build if verification fails.
+
+A local dry-run mode writes the predicate without signing.
+
+### Provenance content
+
+The predicate has this shape. Values in angle brackets vary per build:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "buildType": "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/RELEASE.md#staging-image-provenance-v1",
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    },
+    "resolvedDependencies": [
+      { "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue", "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" } }
+    ]
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" },
+    "metadata": { "invocationId": "https://console.cloud.google.com/cloud-build/builds/<build-id>?project=<project-number>" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+### Failure handling
+
+A failed attestation or self-check step fails the build with a non-zero exit code.
+The artifact stays in the staging registry without an attestation.
+Rerunning the postsubmit signs the artifact again.
+The earlier push stays in the registry, but the promoter does not promote it, because promotion acts only on digests that the current run references.
```

+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+After each image and chart push, the staging build signs a SLSA v1 build provenance attestation as an OCI referrer.
+The signature uses the build's own workload identity.
+The image promoter verifies the attestation when present and carries it to the production registry, next to the promotion signature.
+Consumers verify the attestation against the build identity and the public Sigstore transparency log.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **SLSA** (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts): a framework that defines levels of build provenance assurance. This KEP targets SLSA Build L1, which requires a signed provenance statement from the build system.
+- **Sigstore**: an open-source project providing tools and infrastructure for signing and verifying software artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter.
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+- **OCI referrer**: an artifact attached to an existing image or chart via the OCI referrers API, allowing tools to discover signatures, attestations, and SBOMs associated with a digest without modifying the original artifact.
+- **cosign**: a Sigstore tool for signing and verifying container images and other OCI artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Fulcio / Rekor**: Sigstore components. Fulcio issues short-lived signing certificates tied to a workload identity (OIDC token). Rekor is the public transparency log where certificates and signatures are recorded and made auditable.
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue image they are running
+
+An admin wants to confirm that a running Kueue image was built from a known commit.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+If no attestation is present — because the image predates the feature or the build failed before the attestation step — `cosign` exits with a non-zero status and prints a message such as `no matching attestations`. This is expected for any Kueue image built before the v0.21 Alpha milestone or during an interrupted build.
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+They admit Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present:
+
```

+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+After each image and chart push, the staging build signs a SLSA v1 build provenance attestation as an OCI referrer.
+The signature uses the build's own workload identity.
+The image promoter verifies the attestation when present and carries it to the production registry, next to the promotion signature.
+Consumers verify the attestation against the build identity and the public Sigstore transparency log.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **SLSA** (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts): a framework that defines levels of build provenance assurance. This KEP targets SLSA Build L1, which requires a signed provenance statement from the build system.
+- **Sigstore**: an open-source project providing tools and infrastructure for signing and verifying software artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter.
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+- **OCI referrer**: an artifact attached to an existing image or chart via the OCI referrers API, allowing tools to discover signatures, attestations, and SBOMs associated with a digest without modifying the original artifact.
+- **cosign**: a Sigstore tool for signing and verifying container images and other OCI artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Fulcio / Rekor**: Sigstore components. Fulcio issues short-lived signing certificates tied to a workload identity (OIDC token). Rekor is the public transparency log where certificates and signatures are recorded and made auditable.
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue image they are running
+
+An admin wants to confirm that a running Kueue image was built from a known commit.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+If no attestation is present — because the image predates the feature or the build failed before the attestation step — `cosign` exits with a non-zero status and prints a message such as `no matching attestations`. This is expected for any Kueue image built before the v0.21 Alpha milestone or during an interrupted build.
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+They admit Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: slsaprovenance1
+          signatureFormat: bundle
+```
+
+### Notes/Constraints/Caveats
+
+- The level achieved is SLSA Build L1.
+  The build writes its own provenance predicate, and build steps are not isolated from each other.
+- Attestations attach to the multi-arch index digest that the image promoter references.
+  Platform-specific manifests do not carry their own attestation.
+
+- During Alpha (v0.21), attestations are attached to staging artifacts only.
+  Production-registry (`registry.k8s.io`) images do not carry attestations until the promoter policy change in `kubernetes/k8s.io` lands (Beta). The `cosign verify-attestation` example in Story 1 applies to production images from Beta (v0.22) onward.
+
+### Risks and Mitigations
+
+#### A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases
+
+A staging build cannot sign or verify while Sigstore is unavailable.
+Rerun the postsubmit after the outage.
+Until the promoter policy requires provenance, a missing attestation delays the attestation but does not block promotion.
+
+#### Anyone who can act as the build identity can sign false provenance
+
+Access to the service account is limited to staging project administrators and the Cloud Build pipeline.
+Consumers must pin both the signing identity and the issuer when they verify.
+Consumers must not treat L1 provenance as tamper-proof.
+
+#### An unattested artifact can be promoted during the transition period
+
+The promoter policy starts in warn mode, so an unattested artifact can still be promoted.
+Until the policy requires provenance, the in-build self-check is the enforcement point.
+
+#### Consumers may assume L1 provenance gives stronger guarantees than it does
+
+The consumer documentation, tracked separately, states the SLSA level and its limits.
+
+## Design Details
+
+This KEP changes no Kueue API, configuration, or controller behavior.
+
+### Attested artifacts
+
+| Artifact | Type | Phase |
+|---|---|---|
+| kueue | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-backend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-frontend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| Periodic build images (debug, importer, ray-mini) | Image | Not attested |
+| GitHub release assets | Binary and manifest | Future work |
+
+### Build identity
+
+The staging build runs as a dedicated service account, `kueue-sa`, in the staging project.
+The account already has Artifact Registry write access and OIDC token-creator permissions.
+The build obtains a Fulcio identity certificate from its ambient Google identity, so it needs no extra credentials.
+Consumers verify against the account's email address and the Google OIDC issuer.
+
+### Attestation step
+
+1. After the image and chart pushes complete, resolve each artifact's digest from its tag.
+2. Write a SLSA v1 predicate that records the source repository, git ref, git commit, builder identity, and build invocation ID.
+3. Sign the predicate as a Sigstore bundle OCI referrer, using the build's ambient workload identity.
+4. Verify the attestation against the same digest and identity as an in-build self-check.
+   Fail the build if verification fails.
+
+A local dry-run mode writes the predicate without signing.
+
+### Provenance content
+
+The predicate has this shape. Values in angle brackets vary per build:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "buildType": "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/RELEASE.md#staging-image-provenance-v1",
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    },
+    "resolvedDependencies": [
+      { "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue", "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" } }
+    ]
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" },
+    "metadata": { "invocationId": "https://console.cloud.google.com/cloud-build/builds/<build-id>?project=<project-number>" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+### Failure handling
+
+A failed attestation or self-check step fails the build with a non-zero exit code.
+The artifact stays in the staging registry without an attestation.
+Rerunning the postsubmit signs the artifact again.
+The earlier push stays in the registry.
+Promotion resolves the release tag to a digest, so it can select this unattested digest if the tag still points to it.
+Under `warn` mode the promoted image can lack provenance; setting the policy to `require` prevents promotion of unattested images.
+
+### Promotion
+
+The image promoter verifies the build attestation when present and carries it to the production registry.
+This requires the Kueue provenance policy in the promoter manifest in kubernetes/k8s.io (see [Changes in other repositories](#changes-in-other-repositories)). That change has not landed yet.
+The promotion signature is added after the copy and is unaffected.
+The promoter policy for Kueue starts in `warn` mode.
+After one full release cycle, the policy moves to `require`.
+
+### Release candidates
+
+Release candidate tags trigger the same postsubmit build.
+Release candidates are attested without extra configuration.
+Consumers verify release candidate images the same way as release images.
+
+### Changes in other repositories
+
+| Repository | Change | Required for |
+|---|---|---|
+| kubernetes/test-infra | Submit the postsubmit build as `kueue-sa` | Signing with the Kueue-specific identity |
+| kubernetes/k8s.io | Add a Kueue provenance policy in `warn` mode to the promoter manifest | Carrying attestations to production |
+| kubernetes/k8s.io | Change the policy to `require` after one release | Stable graduation |
+
+These changes are not part of this KEP's implementation PR.
+They are tracked as external follow-ups.
+
+### Interactions
+
+- SBOM and OpenVEX release steps: unchanged. They run in a separate GitHub Actions workflow.
+- Promotion signature: unchanged. It is added at copy time and exists alongside the build provenance.
+- Periodic builds: not covered, because those images are not promoted.
+- Consumer documentation and the release checklist: tracked by the docs sub-issue.
+- GitHub release asset provenance: future work.
+
```

+
+<!-- toc -->

+
+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+After each image and chart push, the staging build signs a SLSA v1 build provenance attestation as an OCI referrer.
+The signature uses the build's own workload identity.
+The image promoter verifies the attestation when present and carries it to the production registry, next to the promotion signature.
+Consumers verify the attestation against the build identity and the public Sigstore transparency log.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **SLSA** (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts): a framework that defines levels of build provenance assurance. This KEP targets SLSA Build L1, which requires provenance from the build system; this KEP also signs it.
+- **Sigstore**: an open-source project providing tools and infrastructure for signing and verifying software artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter.
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+- **OCI referrer**: an artifact attached to an existing image or chart via the OCI referrers API, allowing tools to discover signatures, attestations, and SBOMs associated with a digest without modifying the original artifact.
+- **cosign**: a Sigstore tool for signing and verifying container images and other OCI artifacts using short-lived certificates and a public transparency log.
+- **Fulcio / Rekor**: Sigstore components. Fulcio issues short-lived signing certificates tied to a workload identity (OIDC token). Rekor is the public transparency log where certificates and signatures are recorded and made auditable.
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue image they are running
+
+An admin wants to confirm that a running Kueue image was built from a known commit.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+This command applies to production images from Beta (v0.22) onward.
+During Alpha (v0.21), only staging images carry attestations, so verify `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/kueue@sha256:<digest>` instead.
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v0.21.0",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+If no attestation is present — because the image predates the feature or the build failed before the attestation step — `cosign` exits with a non-zero status and prints a message such as `no matching attestations`. This is expected for any Kueue image built before the v0.21 Alpha milestone or during an interrupted build.
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+They admit Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      signatureFormat: bundle
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
+```
```

+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+They admit Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      signatureFormat: bundle
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
+```
+
+### Notes/Constraints/Caveats
+
+- The level achieved is SLSA Build L1.
+  The build writes its own provenance predicate, and build steps are not isolated from each other.
+- Attestations attach to the multi-arch index digest that the image promoter references.
+  Platform-specific manifests do not carry their own attestation.
+
+- During Alpha (v0.21), attestations are attached to staging artifacts only.
+  Production-registry (`registry.k8s.io`) images do not carry attestations until the promoter policy change in `kubernetes/k8s.io` lands (Beta).
+
+### Risks and Mitigations
+
+#### A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases
+
+A staging build cannot sign or verify while Sigstore is unavailable.
+Rerun the postsubmit after the outage.
+Until the promoter policy requires provenance, a missing attestation delays the attestation but does not block promotion.
+
+#### Anyone who can act as the build identity can sign false provenance
+
+Access to the service account is limited to staging project administrators and the Cloud Build pipeline.
+Consumers must pin both the signing identity and the issuer when they verify.
+Consumers must not treat L1 provenance as tamper-proof.
+
+#### An unattested artifact can be promoted during the transition period
+
+The promoter policy starts in warn mode, so an unattested artifact can still be promoted.
+Until the policy requires provenance, the in-build self-check is the enforcement point.
+
+#### Consumers may assume L1 provenance gives stronger guarantees than it does
+
+The consumer documentation, tracked separately, states the SLSA level and its limits.
+
+## Design Details
+
+This KEP changes no Kueue API, configuration, or controller behavior.
+
+### Attested artifacts
+
+| Artifact | Type | Phase |
+|---|---|---|
+| kueue | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-backend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-frontend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| Periodic build images (debug, importer, ray-mini) | Image | Not attested |
+| GitHub release assets | Binary and manifest | Future work |
+
+### Build identity
+
+The staging build runs as a dedicated service account, `kueue-sa`, in the staging project.
+The account already has Artifact Registry write access and OIDC token-creator permissions.
+The build obtains a Fulcio identity certificate from its ambient Google identity, so it needs no extra credentials.
+Consumers verify against the account's email address and the Google OIDC issuer.
+
+### Attestation step
+
+1. After the image and chart pushes complete, resolve each artifact's digest from its tag.
+2. Write a SLSA v1 predicate that records the source repository, git ref, git commit, builder identity, and build invocation ID.
+3. Sign the predicate as a Sigstore bundle OCI referrer, using the build's ambient workload identity.
+4. Verify the attestation against the same digest and identity as an in-build self-check.
+   Fail the build if verification fails.
+
+A local dry-run mode writes the predicate without signing.
+
+### Provenance content
+
+The predicate has this shape. Values in angle brackets vary per build:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "buildType": "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/RELEASE.md#staging-image-provenance-v1",
```
